Founded in 1984, Mass Precision is a precision metal fabricator and total solutions provider based in Silicon Valley. The company supports customers from initial design and prototyping through full-scale production, with particular expertise in new product introduction (NPI) and high-mix, low-volume manufacturing.

Mass Precision operates multiple facilities across the US, Mexico, and Malaysia. In the first month following full deployment, Mass Precision onboarded more than 40 users to GroundControl and completed over 100 First Article Inspection Reports on a single, shared platform.

Before GroundControl, Mass Precision's AS9102 software was clunky and error-prone with CAD-like menus built for design work rather than first article reporting, and OCR that confused zeros with the letter O.

Catching those mistakes became someone's full-time job. Mass Precision employed a dedicated quality professional whose full-time job was reviewing exported reports for mistakes instead of contributing to higher-value quality work, and the errors were consistent enough that the company was forced to file a formal corrective action.
Mass Precision rolled out GroundControl in the United States and Mexico, bringing both sites onto the platform in close succession.

Rather than deploying to every user simultaneously, GroundControl’s team began with Brenda, who oversees quality operations across both sites, working with Austin at the Guadalajara facility. Once that initial group was proficient, the remaining documentation and reporting staff completed a single cross-site training.

Approximately 40 users now rely on GroundControl daily, working from the same reports in real time regardless of site location. New operators typically became productive on the platform within about 30 minutes of training.
40+ users onboarded in a single rollout, representing the full quality team across both sites.

Mass Precision’s leadership determined that GroundControl paid for itself within the first month of full deployment. Before switching, the quality team completed an average of 54 FAIRs a month, each covering roughly six subassemblies or drawings, for about 324 drawings requiring preparation and ballooning every month.

In that first month of full GroundControl usage, the team completed more than 100 FAIRs, nearly double the previous pace. Mass Precision had previously hired a quality professional whose main focus was reviewing ballooning errors; with GroundControl, the quality team reallocated that resource to work directly with customers.

Mass Precision’s team had grown accustomed to vendors whose software felt like it had never actually been used by the people who built it. GroundControl felt different from the start, an impression reinforced when the GroundControl team traveled on-site to meet Mass Precision’s staff in person, learn how their facilities operate, and understand their workflows firsthand.
Mass Precision’s team praised training delivered by the GroundControl team as straightforward and genuinely easy to follow.

A First Article Inspection (FAI) is a documented, characteristic-by-character verification that your first production run meets all drawing and specification requirements. In aerospace, AS9102 defines how you plan, execute, and record that verification using Forms 1-3, plus linked objective evidence.
